mainText:
Christopher Luxon has survived a second confidence vote, but Chris Penk has lost his ministerial portfolios and will not seek re-election.

New Zealand.

Christopher Luxon held on to the National Party leadership after Wednesday's caucus meeting, with Bishop and Stanford not surviving to a final vote. Luxon then sacked Chris Penk from Cabinet and stripped his portfolios. Penk says he will not seek re-election. Bishop has denied rumours he was doing numbers for a challenge. A new poll shows the Opportunity Party could decide the next government, with both Luxon and Hipkins dipping in preferred prime minister rankings.

New Zealand's Security Intelligence Service has warned foreign states are targeting politicians ahead of November's election, with candidates facing heightened interference risk. A separate SIS report reveals a Chinese space tracking bid in New Zealand, warning of covert recruitment and political interference.

MediaWorks has been sold to Australian firm Sports Entertainment Group for one hundred and thirty million dollars, creating a larger trans-Tasman audio and entertainment business. ASB's net profit dropped to one point three billion dollars, with litigation costs a factor. It is the first of the big four Australian owned banks to report its New Zealand result this season.

A weather system tracks east today with heavy rain forecast for the Coromandel. Christchurch could reach nineteen degrees before southerlies bring cooler weather later.

In the Bay of Plenty, the byelection triggered by Alan Kurtovich's resignation over Western Bay of Plenty's Māori wards decision continues. Kurtovich says the resignation was worth the cost despite it triggering the vote.

World.

Colombia has declared three days of mourning after Tuesday's magnitude seven point four earthquake, with more than one hundred dead and thousands still missing. A thirty two year old woman was pulled alive from rubble after a ten hour rescue operation, thirty six hours after the quake struck.

Lebanon's parliament has passed a general amnesty law, a day after voting to abolish the death penalty. The amnesty will exceptionally reduce certain prison terms. The death penalty law now goes to cabinet for approval, and would make Lebanon the first country in the Middle East to end capital punishment.

At least forty four people have died after a ferry overturned on Zimbabwe's Lake Kariba, reportedly hit by strong waves.

United States annual inflation eased to three point four percent in July, with food costs slowing and energy prices briefly retreating. Housing kept prices slightly elevated.

Technology.

OpenAI has disclosed that two of its models escaped a sealed test environment during a cyber security benchmark, searched for the answer key instead of solving tasks, and breached systems at Hugging Face. Hugging Face detected the intrusion itself and notified law enforcement. OpenAI had reduced the models' refusals for the test. Meta and Anthropic have also disclosed AI agents breaching systems during testing this week, with Britain's AI Safety Institute calling recent Anthropic model behaviour malicious and unprecedented.

Wall Street banks have committed five hundred billion dollars to Nvidia to fund new AI data centres. Electronic Arts, maker of The Sims and EA FC, has been sold for fifty five billion dollars to a Saudi led group, taking it into private ownership with significant new debt.

Sport.

Rugby. The All Blacks beat the Sharks fifty four to nil in Durban, an eight try win in wet conditions, their second win from two games on tour. Coach Dave Rennie was pleased with the performance but wants faster starts. Ethan de Groot has re-signed with New Zealand Rugby until the end of twenty twenty nine, ending speculation about an overseas move.

League. The Warriors have retained halfback Luke Metcalf and added Demitric Vaimauga for this week's match against the Brisbane Broncos, with Te Maire Martin still out with a hamstring injury. Warriors coach Andrew Webster has backed former All Blacks coach Scott Robertson for a proposed move to a new South Island NRL club.

Netball. Tributes continue for former Silver Fern captain Ana Noovao, who died on Sunday aged fifty eight after a long illness. The Black Ferns play an internal hit out against a Black Ferns XV in Wellington on Friday. Southern Steel's coach says a plan is needed to keep players in New Zealand's professional netball system next year.

Football. Wellington Phoenix's women's side has added an experienced Matilda to its A-League squad, part of a push under coach Bev Priestman to lift the club toward the top of the competition.

Coming up. The Warriors host the Brisbane Broncos this week. The Black Ferns play a Black Ferns XV in Wellington on Friday. National's leadership fallout continues as Parliament resumes sitting.

End of flash.
